diff of v15-quick vs v16-full frozen tests: polish/visual judge.toml and all scored prompt.md identical; functional judge.toml differs in Stop/supersede timing procedure, preview isolation, save/restart and history criteria
evidence: Every interactive, time-varying and viewport promise in the brief has a judge instruction to act, not a still first paint. Viewport: polish cw_narrow_width_usable says 'Resize the browser viewport to about 390 by 844 pixels and reload', scroll vertically to the five areas, type and press Run there, then restore desktop. Visual prompt.md:13-14 sets 1440x900, makes the judge Run a ten-line draft, 'watch the caret for about two seconds, because a caret may blink', and double-click a word before the screenshots. Time: functional prompt.md:27 says 'Where waiting is required, wait the stated time; do not shorten it'. The criteria wait 8 s after the budget (cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_newer_run_supersedes), up to 10 s for time-limit reasons and live library refresh, and give a 10 s idle baseline before the newer-revision notice. Stop and supersede races use one code-runner action with void-and-retry rules. Interaction: all criteria use real keys, clicks, drags and modifier-clicks (app_context.md:18-21), including clicking buttons inside the preview (cw_html_preview, cw_last_good_recovery, cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget), keyboard focus traversal (cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus) and scroll-following (cw_caret_kept_in_view, cw_long_line_editing, cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state). The brief has no theme toggle or hover requirement, so theming does not apply. Runtime: the hosted v15 Oracle run (kTaeUNx, hashes verified) shows judges actually resizing ('Resized to 390x844 and reloaded ... scrollWidth = clientWidth = 390 ... Desktop viewport restored to 1280x720'), catching caret 'blink phases' and waiting a '10s idle baseline'. The polish and visual judge.toml and prompt.md bytes are identical in v16. The scripted golden (polish.cjs:111-130, results/polish.json cw_narrow_width_usable true) is not judge evidence. Remaining risk: no configured judge run exists on the v16 bytes. The v16 functional criteria changed the Stop and newer-Run timing procedure to a Playwright code-runner wait-then-click with up to three attempts, and whether the frozen judge can carry it out is unmeasured. A minor conforming-alternative risk also remains. cw_controls_feedback_and_labels does not tell the judge to read feedback immediately, so a brief toast that disappears before a later snapshot could be missed. Playwright MCP usually snapshots right after the click, which lessens this.
